issue: English grammar: 'answer ... to this question' is ungrammatical (one answers a question, or gives an answer to it); the stacked commas also make the aside hard to read.
russian: поспешил сердито ответить Бездомный на этот, признаться, не очень ясный вопрос
old: Bezdomny hurried to answer angrily to this, admittedly, not very clear question.
new: Bezdomny hastened to give an angry answer to this question, which, admittedly, was not very clear.

issue: Grammatical-gender calque: «это она, опять она» refers to «болезнь» (feminine). English 'it’s her, her again' turns the illness into a woman, which the Russian does not do.
russian: это она, опять она, непобедимая, ужасная болезнь
old: it’s her, her again, the invincible, terrible illness
new: it’s that, that again, the invincible, terrible illness

issue: Wrong gender for Banga: «пожаловаться ей» agrees grammatically with «собаку», but Banga is a male dog, and modern-en itself calls him 'he/his' throughout ch. 26 (26:5, 26:79).
old: complain to her about the hemicrania
new: complain to him about the hemicrania

issue: Capitalisation of a title used as address: ch. 1 writes 'Professor' in the vocative (1:73, 1:126, 1:141), as with 'Procurator'. Ch. 3 lowercases it in the same scene. (Lower case is reserved for hegemon/messire/donna in GLOSSARY.md.)
Calque of «убедиться» ('saw / satisfied themselves'). 'Made sure' means 'ensured' in English, so it reads as if the friends caused his eye to be mad.
russian: убедились в том, что левый, зеленый, у него совершенно безумен
old: and they made sure that his left eye
new: and saw for themselves that his left eye

issue: Capitalisation of 'Professor' in address; same issue as 3:7 (ch. 1 uses 'Professor').
Capitalisation of 'Professor' in address; same issue as 3:7.
Tautology that the Russian lacks: 'his little eyes were small'. «глазки маленькие» is a single diminutive idea.
old: his little eyes were small, ironic and half drunk
new: his eyes were tiny, ironic and half drunk

issue: Probable mistranslation. «алую повязку» on the driver, the 'Komsomol girl' of 1:100, seen together with her white face, is her red kerchief or headscarf (the Komsomol emblem), not an armband. The white face and red kerchief are meant as one image.
russian: совершенно белое от ужаса лицо женщины-вагоновожатой и ее алую повязку

issue: Calque of «убедился» ('saw / became convinced'). 'Made sure' means 'ensured'.
russian: заглянув ему в лицо, убедился в том, что никаких признаков сумасшествия в этом лице нет и не было
old: made sure that there were not, and never had been,
new: saw that there were not, and never had been,

issue: Wrong sense. «убедился» means 'he realized at once'. 'At once made sure that it would be very hard to catch up' says Ivan arranged for the chase to fail.
russian: тотчас убедился, что догнать их будет очень трудно
old: and at once made sure that it would be very hard
new: and at once realized that it would be very hard

issue: Unclear referent. The doorman's deferential plural «их ... они — член» comes out as 'them' with no gloss, so the reader looks for a group (the ladies?). In 4:21 and 7:87 the plural of respect is either explained or rendered as 'the gentleman'.
russian: как же я могу их не допустить, если они — член Массолита?
old: how can I refuse them entry, if the gentleman is a member of Massolit?
new: how can I refuse the gentleman entry, if he is a member of Massolit?

issue: Spelling consistency: HARMONISATION.md unified 'Good-bye' to 'goodbye'. This is the only hyphenated form left in the edition (13 other uses of 'goodbye').

Ambiguous referent. «гражданки Беломут» is the wife, but 'Citizen Belomut' in English reads as the husband, who vanished in 7:10. The feminine «гражданка» is lost here. The edition uses 'citizeness' elsewhere (3:3, 4:49).
russian: она не застала уже гражданки Беломут в квартире
old: she found Citizen Belomut no longer in the apartment
new: she found Citizeness Belomut no longer in the apartment

issue: Stiff passive a reader stumbles on: 'it was moved into—by'. The Russian is an ordinary active «в нее вселились — покойный Берлиоз…».
russian: а затем в нее вселились — покойный Берлиоз с супругой и этот самый Степа тоже с супругой
old: and then it was moved into—by the late Berlioz and his wife, and by this same Styopa, also with his wife.
new: and then in moved—the late Berlioz with his wife, and this same Styopa, also with his wife.

issue: Calque of «вход его получился … торжественным»: in English an entrance does not 'come out' solemn.
russian: и вход его получился поэтому очень торжественным
old: and so his entrance came out very solemn
new: and so his entrance was a very solemn one

issue: Calque that can mean the opposite. «на редкость умные» means 'exceptionally clever', but 'rarely clever' reads as 'seldom clever'.
russian: среди интеллигентов тоже попадаются на редкость умные
old: you come across some rarely clever ones
new: you come across some exceptionally clever ones

issue: Unidiomatic reply. «Совершенно правильно!» answers 'Have I understood you correctly?' and means 'Quite right!'. 'Perfectly correctly!' is not English.
